approach: Use the standard equations for motion under constant gravity, taking upward as positive and deceleration g.

steps.text: Maximum height uses the equation relating v² to u² with v = 0 at the top.
Substitute the values to find the maximum height.
Time to reach maximum height uses v = u − gt with v = 0 at the top.
Half the maximum height is 62.5 m; use v² = u² − 2gh with this height to find the speed there.
Take the square root to get the speed at half the maximum height.
steps.why_this_step: This is the last unknown asked for, completing the three parts.

common_mistakes.text: Finding the speed at half the time to the top instead of half the height, using v = u − g(t/2) = 50 − 25 = 25 m/s, which answers a different question.
Dropping the factor of 2 in v² = u² − 2gh and using v² = u² − gh, which gives about 43.3 m/s instead of 35.36 m/s.
